(a) «aprobación independiente del autor del PR» needs a second person, and GitHub does not let a PR author approve her own PR. (b) Branch protection, rulesets and environment required reviewers are free only on **public** repos; private repos need a paid plan. (c) Artifact attestations (`actions/attest-build-provenance`) are likewise free only on public repos. (d) «demuestra rollback en staging» and a canary «al 10%» need a deployed service with traffic. The course has not given her one, and the You Do forbids «servicios externos obligatorios». GitHub Actions itself is free on public repos, but S01–S43 never showed a real workflow file (0 hits for `.github/workflows` before S44), and S44 only models one as a Python string.

(2) Use the exact workflow YAML (checkout pinned by SHA, `setup-python`, ruff/mypy/pytest matrix, `upload-artifact`, `cyclonedx-py` or `syft` for the SBOM, `attest-build-provenance`). (3) Use an environment `staging` with herself as reviewer, and state plainly that this is not independent approval (record a peer or mentor review as an alternative). issues.description:

CP-N3-C (`BRIEF.md`, `RUBRIC.json.tests_required`, `catalog.ts`) requires «baseline determinista», «calibración reportada», «umbral por costo → revisión humana», «no fuga de datos» (train/eval separation), «desempeño por subgrupo», «abstención soportada» and the interface `triage.score(case) -> TriageDecision`. Its P0s include «Sin calibración» and «Fuga de datos». The S39 You Do starter's "model" is `score = min(1.0, 0.35 + 0.45 * bool(case["shared_signal"]))`. It has no training data, no baseline, no calibration, no cost-based threshold, no split and no per-subgroup performance, and it exposes `triage(case, *, threshold, …) -> Tuple`. S39's own tagline promises «con baseline, calibración, abstención». Calibration and baselines were taught in S33–S35 (grep `calibra` S34: 99 hits, `baseline` S33: 97), but S39 never asks her to reuse them.

issues.title: [S37-R02] S37 The You Do's core gate, «¿es más rápido, y sigue dando lo mismo?», is tautological and cannot fail.
issues.description:
[O] The You Do's core gate, «¿es más rápido, y sigue dando lo mismo?», is tautological and cannot fail. `before_path` and `after_path` both end with `return match_score(values)`, computed over all values whatever their pair loops did, and the loops only assign `_ = …`. `ok_same` is therefore `True` by construction, so the `assert ok_same` can never trigger. Blocking drops about 90% of pairs with no recall check, though objective 1 says «sin abandonar el recall como gate de matching». The section teaches that blocking has a recall cost (`theory[0].paragraphs[3]`) and then hands her a fixture where that cost is invisible.

Dónde (campo del contenido): `youDo.starterCode` (`before_path`, `after_path`, `ok_same`), `youDo.objectives[1]`
issues.actual: Evidencia: «for j in range(i + 1, len(block)):\n                _ = block[i] + block[j]\n    return match_score(values)»
issues.improvement: `src/lib/course/sections/s37-dbt-bigquery.ts`: have both paths return the *set of matched pairs*, e.g. `(i, j)` with `abs(values[i]-values[j]) <= 2` over shuffled synthetic records with a block key. Compute `same_result = before == after` and `recall = len(after & before) / len(before)`, and include a key choice that loses matches so the gate can go red. (A gate that cannot fail is a tautological test; AGENTS.md calls these worse than no test.)

issues.description:

issues.description:

The You Do labels `y=[1,1,0,0]` are exactly a tie, so this matters. `max(set(y), key=y.count)` returns the first maximal element in set-iteration order. issues.description:
[I] The You Do's core method is likely to crash the first time Lucía tests it, and nothing on the page explains why. `insert_decision_with_evidence` must do «BEGIN → decisión → lastrowid → evidence → COMMIT», as every demo does with `con.execute("BEGIN")`. Every demo issues `BEGIN` right after DDL, where Python's `sqlite3` has no transaction open. In the You Do she must first seed `entities` and `candidate_pairs` with ordinary `INSERT`s, which (by default) silently open an implicit transaction. Her explicit `BEGIN` then raises `OperationalError: cannot start a transaction within a transaction`. A grep of S12 and S29 finds 0 hits for `isolation_level`, `autocommit` or «implícit».

Dónde (campo del contenido): `youDo.starterCode` (`insert_decision_with_evidence` comment), `youDo.requirements[6]`, `theory[6].code`

issues.title: [S20-R01] S20 The You Do's central gate checks nothing.
issues.description:
[O] The You Do's central gate checks nothing. In the starter, `portada` is read back from `Salida!B1`, the cell `materialize_salida` just filled with `det_sum`, and `n_xlsx` is read back from the `n_rows` it just wrote. `reconcile(det_sum, portada, …)` therefore compares a number with itself. It catches only "forgot to write the cell", never a wrong sum. The same goes for idempotency: `"idempotent": dig_a == dig_b` digests the same `rows` list reversed, and `dig_rows` sorts first, so the result is True by construction. The process is never run twice. Theory promises the opposite: «aquí se comprueba corriendo el proceso dos veces y comparando». The `backup` copies the fresh `out` straight after copying the master, so it is not a backup of a previous result. Lucía will see `reconcile_ok True` and `idempotent True` whether her code is right or not.

Dónde (campo del contenido): `youDo.starterCode` (steps 3–5), `theory[0].paragraphs[3]`
issues.actual: Evidencia: «portada = sal["B1"].value if sal["B1"].value is not None else -1.0» / «dig_b = dig_rows(list(reversed(rows)))  # mismo multiconjunto, otro orden»
issues.improvement: `src/lib/course/sections/s20-rag.ts`: reconcile against an independent source, either a `pd.read_csv` of the synthetic input or a `portada` cell the template already holds, and include one deliberately wrong fixture that must print `reconcile_ok False`. Prove idempotency by running `run_factory(input)` twice and comparing `dig_rows` of the two `Salida` sheets read back from disk. Back up the *previous* `results.xlsx` before overwriting it. (AGENTS.md treats tautological checks as worse than none, and this one sits in the deliverable.)

issues.description:

issues.title: [S08-R01] S08 The section gives two opposite "only" contracts for atomic writes.
issues.description:
[O] The section gives two opposite "only" contracts for atomic writes. theory[3].paragraphs[1] first says «contrato único del curso, no hay otro: `tmp = path.with_name(path.name + ".tmp")`». The same paragraph then says a fixed `.tmp` name reintroduces the failure atomic writing was meant to prevent, and that the temp name must be unique per run. The theory code and callout use `tempfile.mkstemp` («Contrato del curso: temporal unico por corrida (mkstemp…)»). Meanwhile iDo.steps[1], weDo.steps[4–5], the theory[11] checklist («¿tmp es `name + ".tmp"`?»), `youDo.requirements[7]` and `selfCheck.questions[1]` all require the fixed name. Lucía is graded on the pattern the theory calls broken.

Dónde (campo del contenido): `theory[3].paragraphs[1]`, `theory[3].code`, `theory[3].callout.content`, `theory[11].paragraphs[2]`, `iDo.steps[1]`, `weDo.steps[4].preamble`, `youDo.requirements[7]`, `selfCheck.questions[1].explanation`
issues.actual: Evidencia: «contrato único del curso, no hay otro» vs «Con un `.tmp` fijo, dos ejecuciones simultáneas … publica el contenido a medias de la otra»
issues.improvement: `src/lib/course/sections/s08-files-ingestion.ts`: choose one. Either teach the simple fixed `.tmp` and state its single-writer limit as a named trade-off, or make `mkstemp(dir=path.parent)` the contract in iDo, We Do, You Do, checklist and self-check (a contract that contradicts itself cannot be learned or assessed).

[O] The section says it will not teach conditionals, loops, functions or error recovery, yet the We Do and the You Do require her to write all four, plus `dict`, `assert` and the `if __name__ == "__main__"` guard. Nothing in S01 or S02 teaches these, so Lucía cannot do the "independent" and "transfer" exercises from understanding. She can only copy the I Do demo, which turns a construction task into transcription.

Dónde (campo del contenido): `theory[0].paragraphs[5]` and `theory[0].callout` versus `weDo.steps[4].instruction`, `weDo.steps[5]`, `weDo.steps[17]`, `weDo.steps[23]`, `youDo.requirements[4]`, `youDo.requirements[7]`
issues.actual: Evidencia: «en S02 prepararás sus piezas básicas sin adelantar condicionales, bucles, funciones ni recuperación de errores» versus «Completa el cuerpo de `safe_int` (vacío tras strip → error; `try int`; `ValueError` → mensaje)» and «Incluye una función `main()` y el guard `if __name__ == "__main__"`»
issues.reproductionSteps:
1. Abrir S02 (basics)
2. Pestaña youdo
3. Ubicar `theory[0].paragraphs[5]` and `theory[0].callout` versus `weDo.steps[4].instruction`, `weDo.steps[5]`, `weDo.steps[17]`, `weDo.steps[23]`, `youDo.requirements[4]`, `youDo.requirements[7]`
issues.improvement: `src/lib/course/sections/s02-basics.ts`: either (a) add a short "sintaxis de apoyo" theory block that teaches `def/return`, `if/else`, `for`, `try/except ValueError`, dict literals and `assert` at reading level, and remove the «sin adelantar…» promise; or (b) re-scope weDo E2/E3 and the You Do to straight-line code (raw/clean/convert/print) and move `safe_int`/`parse_client` to S03/S05. Constructive alignment needs the activities to use only what was taught. The section's own hidden contract even admits the gap: «"if_for_as_support_syntax": True».
